Liverpool begin their Champions League campaign at home as they host Atletico Madrid at Anfield. These sides met at Anfield on matchday one last season, with Liverpool winning a dramatic game 3-2. Liverpool led 2-0 inside the opening 10 minutes before Atletico came back to level the game at 2-2. Virgil van Dijk then scored in added time to give Liverpool all three points before Atletico boss Diego Simeone was sent off for clashing with the Anfield crowd, resulting in a one-match ban.

Andoni Iraola earned his first win as Liverpool boss on Friday night as they won 2-0 away at Ipswich thanks to a quickfire early double from Alexander Isak. This will be Iraola’s first Champions League match as a manager.

“I think obviously it is a special night for me,” Iraola said. “Everyone talks [about] the Champions League nights at Anfield and also the first game is against a strong opposition, it is Atletico Madrid. [Diego] Simeone is doing an incredible job as a manager. To be all the years that he has been achieving every season the goals of the club I think is remarkable and definitely it is a big challenge for us. I think I played against him as a player, he was still a player, and I played against his teams when he was a coach and I also coached against him. So, we had a lot of precedent before. Definitely he has much more experience than me in this kind of games but I hope tomorrow we can give him a good game.

“It is one of the dreams, probably, when you start. It was difficult for me when I started my coaching career seven, eight years ago, to position myself in the position that I am right now, and I hope I can enjoy it. It is a big responsibility, massive challenge, but I feel privileged to be there in that dugout tomorrow [tonight] and now my thinking is about putting the team together in a position where we can play a good game, win the game and start strong in this Champions League.”

Atletico Madrid currently sit sixth in La Liga and suffered their first defeat on Saturday as they lost 3-0 at Athletic Bilbao. They did reach the semi-finals of the Champions League last season, where they fell to Arsenal 2-1 on aggregate.

“We are coming into a marvellous stadium and there will be a great atmosphere,” Simeone said. “We will have to look good from the start of the game because it will be full on. He [Andoni Iraola] works very well with the team, focusing on the tactical awareness of each player. It takes time to find the right path, but he is growing and improving and he has some very good players.”

Team news from Anfield to follow shortly.

#1550. Chelsea targeting Trent Alexander-Arnold as surprise transfer opportunity emerges

Barnaby Lane is a highly experienced sports writer who has written for The Times, FourFourTwo Magazine, Sports Illustrated, TalkSPORT, and Business Insider. Over the years, he's had the pleasure of interviewing some of the biggest names in world sport, including Usain Bolt, Rafael Nadal, Christian Pulisic, and more.

Chelsea could be preparing for a significant change at right-back as the club assess their options ahead of the upcoming transfer windows.

With uncertainty surrounding Malo Gusto’s future at Stamford Bridge, the Blues have reportedly identified an unexpected target who could bring considerable experience and creativity to their defence.

Real Madrid defender Trent Alexander-Arnold has emerged as a potential option, with former Manchester United chief scout Mick Brown suggesting the England international could be tempted by a move to west London if Chelsea decide to make an approach.

According to Football Insider, Chelsea are keeping tabs on Alexander-Arnold as questions continue over his role at Real Madrid. The 28-year-old has struggled to establish himself as a regular starter under Jose Mourinho, with competition for places limiting his opportunities.

Brown revealed that Chelsea are among the clubs monitoring the situation, telling Football Insider: “One name who I have heard in connection with a move to Chelsea is Trent Alexander-Arnold.”

He admitted the potential transfer had initially surprised him, adding: “It came as a bit of a surprise to me, to be honest, but he has fallen well down the pecking order at Real Madrid to the point where he’s now the second or even third choice.”

The former scout also questioned whether the defender currently fits into Mourinho’s plans, explaining:

“It appears Mourinho doesn’t rate him particularly in that right-back position, and he’s not the only one, because he’s been out in the cold for England as well.”

Despite those concerns, Brown believes Alexander-Arnold remains an attractive player because of his technical ability and reputation. Chelsea, meanwhile, have reportedly been assessing potential replacements for Gusto as they consider changes to their defensive options.

Brown added: “Alexander-Arnold is a talented footballer who has a very good skillset, but it is those weaknesses in his game that often raises concerns.”

He also suggested that Chelsea’s interest in high-profile players could make the move possible: “Chelsea, though, will always be keen on the possibility of signing a big-name player; it’s just what they do, so they’ll be keeping an eye on whether he does become available.”

The possibility of a return to Liverpool has also been discussed, but Brown believes Stamford Bridge could become a realistic destination if the defender decides to leave Spain.

“They’ll want to avoid that situation coming up again, as will he I expect, so Chelsea could be where he ends up and he could be tempted if they decide to make a move.”

However, Alexander-Arnold is not currently pushing for an exit. Previous reporting has suggested he wants to fight for his place at Real Madrid, meaning any potential Chelsea move would depend on how his situation develops.

#1549. ‘He looks like Rudiger’ - former coach on Real Madrid youngster Lamini Fati

By Alexis Pereira | 03 Nov 2026 22:25, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 23:00

Real Madrid already have a ‘mini-Rudiger’ in Castilla defender Lamini Fati, according to his former coach. Manolo Rueda, who managed the 20-year-old in Leganes’ Under-19s, has told AS that he sees a future Real Madrid first-team centre-back.

Fati is a jewel of La Fabrica. The Spain youth centre-back joined the academy in the summer of 2025 from Leganes and has already made his first appearances for the senior team under boss Jose Mourinho in pre-season.

After starting the season on the bench, Fati has played the last three Castilla games and made his first start against Algeciras (2-0) on 25 October. He was already mentioned in March as a possible solution to a defensive injury crisis, but he appears to need to establish himself in the reserves before hoping to join Mourinho’s squad.

Rueda explained Fati’s characteristics. ‘The quality that stands out most is the security and power he brings to the game. And a characteristic that I think is very underrated is his heading. I think he is very, very, very good in the air in attack. He scores goals and, defensively, he is very forceful.’

To break into Real Madrid’s defensive rotation, Fati has some points to improve. ‘I think Lamini has to bring continuity and speed in actions with the ball,’ Rueda said. ‘Without the ball, he has everything he needs. He has to refine some technical and tactical aspects, but he will get there with age, games and accumulated minutes.’

The 46-year-old sees a bright future. ‘Real Madrid currently have two excellent centre-backs in their squad, Konate and Rudiger. He looks a lot like them and could pair up with either. That is why I think he has a genuine chance of becoming a starting defender at Real Madrid.’

Fati may not get the chance to partner Rudiger, whose contract runs out at the end of the season, aged 33, but he could potentially replace him. ‘He is a player who looks like Rudiger,’ Rueda said. ‘He is aggressive in duels and simplifies actions with the ball. Both have very clear ideas and can execute their tasks at a very high level. Lamini needs to reach that level. If he can reproduce those efforts and behaviours at excellence, we could see “a mini-Rudiger”.’

#1548. Manchester United targeting Dominic Calvert-Lewin in surprise January transfer move

Barnaby Lane is a highly experienced sports writer who has written for The Times, FourFourTwo Magazine, Sports Illustrated, TalkSPORT, and Business Insider. Over the years, he's had the pleasure of interviewing some of the biggest names in world sport, including Usain Bolt, Rafael Nadal, Christian Pulisic, and more.

Manchester United could be forced to strengthen their attacking options in January after another injury setback involving Benjamin Sesko.

With Michael Carrick needing additional firepower to maintain competition for places up front, an experienced Premier League striker has reportedly emerged as a surprise target.

Leeds United forward Dominic Calvert-Lewin is among the names being considered by United’s recruitment team. However, attempting to sign a key player from one of their biggest rivals could prove extremely difficult.

According to The Athletic, Manchester United are exploring the January market for centre-forwards, with Calvert-Lewin one of the players under consideration.

The 29-year-old England international has reportedly been on United’s radar for some time, and recruitment staff are now assessing whether a potential transfer would be feasible when the window opens.

The interest comes amid concerns over Benjamin Sesko’s availability. The Slovenian striker is expected to miss an extended period with a shin injury, leaving Carrick with fewer recognised centre-forward options.

Calvert-Lewin has rebuilt his career since joining Leeds on a free transfer from Everton in 2025. His performances at Elland Road have attracted renewed attention, with the striker scoring 20 goals in 49 appearances for the club across all competitions.

He has also returned to England international contention following his improved form, making him an appealing option for United as they consider their attacking requirements.

However, there are significant obstacles. Leeds are reportedly keen to reward Calvert-Lewin with a new contract, despite his current agreement running until 2028. The club are also understood to be protective of a player who has become an important part of Daniel Farke’s side.

The rivalry between Leeds and Manchester United presents another major complication. A transfer between the clubs would attract considerable attention, and reports suggest the possibility of an agreement is currently remote.

Calvert-Lewin could offer United a different profile in attack, bringing physical presence, aerial ability and considerable Premier League experience. His availability could become particularly important if Sesko remains sidelined into the January window.

United have previously considered alternative centre-forward options, but the latest developments could encourage the recruitment department to widen its search. Calvert-Lewin’s experience in English football would potentially make him an attractive short-term solution.

Nevertheless, Leeds are unlikely to make negotiations straightforward. They have little reason to weaken their squad midway through the campaign, particularly by allowing an important player to join their historic rivals.

United must also consider whether pursuing Calvert-Lewin is realistic when other striker targets may be easier to acquire.

For now, the reported interest represents an option under consideration rather than an imminent transfer. Sesko’s injury has increased the urgency surrounding United’s search for attacking reinforcements, but persuading Leeds to sell their striker could prove a significant challenge.

#1547. Former Liverpool defender Stephen Warnock reveals he hid seizures from club because he was 'petrified' of being released as youngster

Published: 19:09 EDT, 1 November 2026 | Updated: 19:15 EDT, 1 November 2026

Former Liverpool defender Stephen Warnock has revealed he hid seizures from the club out of fear that the Reds would axe him.

Warnock, 44, played 67 times for Liverpool and has transitioned into broadcasting since retiring from playing in 2018.

He suffered from a number of epileptic fits as a youngster - a condition that affects around one in every 100 people.

Warnock never understood what was causing his seizures and told 5 Live: 'I was petrified of telling Liverpool because I was worried about being released. Because I was thinking "if they think I've got a condition they will release me".

'I was worried about being on the pitch and it happens. There were no triggers for me, I never knew what triggered it. That was what petrified me.'

Warnock experienced the seizures for around three years and underwent a number of tests including a CT and MRI scan.

Stephen Warnock, pictured working as a broadcaster, revealed he suffered from seizures

The former Liverpool defender, pictured in action for the Reds back in 2005, said he was terrified of telling the club about his health issue

'I was at a computer and then I woke up in a hospital bed,' he went on. 'And I was like "wow, how have I got here?". I didn't remember anything, I completely blacked out.

'My friends told me I started having a seizure. Obviously an ambulance was called and I was taken to a hospital bed.

'I was embarrassed to be honest, because no-one else had it, no-one knew about it, I didn't know about it until it happened.'

The risk of having a seizure can be reduced with medication and Warnock has not experienced one since he was 14.

'I was in a fortunate position where I grew out of it,' he said.

'I didn't have to go on medication or worry about driving a car or things like that. It's the first time I've ever really spoken about it.'

Warnock, a left-back, departed Liverpool in 2007 and went on to play for Aston Villa, Leeds and Derby among other sides.

He has appeared on a number of television channels while working as a pundit, including the BBC, Sky Sports, BT Sport, NBC and DAZN.

#1546. Barcelona eye Arsenal’s Hincapie as January centre-back option

By Alexis Pereira | 03 Nov 2026 22:37

Barcelona, also recently linked with Paris SG Willian Pacho, have contacted the representatives of Arsenal defender Piero Hincapie as they plan to sign a centre-back in the January transfer window, with boss Hansi Flick said to approve of the Ecuadorian’s profile.

Barcelona are already looking ahead to the winter market, which opens in a little under two months. A first shortlist of four names has been revealed, featuring Alessandro Bastoni, Josko Gvardiol, Natan and Lisandro Martinez, but Actualite Barca, relayed by Sport, says Hincapie is also a target.

Hincapie signed permanently for Arsenal last summer for £34m, after a season on loan with the Gunners. Despite that and the absence of William Saliba since the start of the campaign, the 24-year-old has played little, making seven appearances with only two starts.

His profile still matches what Barcelona want. Flick likes his versatility between centre-back and left-back, a quality that could prove useful if Alejandro Balde leaves in January, as expected.

Sporting director Deco has already established first contact with the player’s entourage, aiming to gauge his willingness to move and explore a winter exit.

The deal will not be simple, however. Boss Mikel Arteta does not view Hincapie, who came from Bayer Leverkusen in 2024, as a regular starter, but he values the player and will be reluctant to let him leave mid-season. Arsenal will also not want to take a loss on the transfer, so they would ask for at least £34m, a significant sum for Barcelona’s finances.

As La Gazzetta dello Sport write, Milan are evolving on an almost game-by-game basis, but the only one who remains the same is Ramos. One factor stands out above all: the Portuguese fails to get into the flow of play, not only when the team is struggling but even when they play well and win.

His derby stats tragically mirror those reported the previous Wednesday against Bologna: zero shots on target, zero shots off target, zero blocked shots, zero chances created, zero assists. The same story. Even the number of balls played was identical: 31.

Yet they were two very different games. Against Inter, Gonçalo even infuriated Luka Modric, who shortly after the quarter-hour mark unleashed a sharp, angled right-footer that was aimed squarely at Josep Martinez. Ramos was right in the path of the ball, potentially denying a 3-0 goal.

Modric muttered words of frustration under his breath, knowing of course that it was not deliberate sabotage. That incident is proof that there are times when nothing goes right, not even when everyone else is playing with a smile.

Ramos’s first two months resemble Gimenez’s a year ago: just as Santiago couldn’t score but had Massimiliano Allegri’s trust thanks to his backroom work for the team, the same is true for Gonçalo. Unlike Santiago, he has scored three goals, though one was a penalty and one a gift.

In terms of goalscoring, his contribution is completely inadequate compared to expectations, the player’s level, and the club’s investment in bringing him to Milanello. Ramos runs, he battles and he tries to get the team moving forward but he can’t get fully involved.

You can also look at it from the other angle: is it the team that are incapable of giving him service? Perhaps precisely because he’s a striker who roams widely and provides no reference points not only for opposing defenders, but also for his own team-mates.

In any case, he was and remains the starting centre-forward. Partly because Francesco Camarda – in Amorim’s eyes – clearly doesn’t offer enough guarantees, and partly because of Gonçalo’s dirty work, which serves to free up space for others.

It’s no coincidence that Adrien Rabiot is frequently finding the back of the net, and the same goes for Diego Moreira and Alphadjo Cisse, all players who don’t usually hang around in the box.

Furthermore, Milan have recently developed a particular quality: when their shots hit the target, they end up in the back of the net. The two goals against Bologna came with their first two shots, the three against Inter with their first three.

Between the Emilians and the Nerazzurri, Milan have had a total of seven shots on target, squeezing five goals from them: a stratospheric 71%. The million-dollar question, now that Milan are poised for the Scudetto race, is: if Ramos were to unlock himself, how far can this team go?
